newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican quake registers 6.7 but no damage reported.
newsitem.headline: Mexican quake registers 6.7 but no damage reported.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale hit the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Mexico on Thursday, the U.S. Geological Survey said.
No damage or injuries were reported.
The seismological service of the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) said in a tape-recorded message that the quake reached 7.0 on the Richter scale at 6:37 a.m. (1137 GMT).
But it was barely felt by Mexicans nearest the epicentre, about 175 miles (280 km) southwest of the coastal resort city of Puerto Vallarta, residents and the local Red Cross said.
"It was felt, but it was very light," Jessica Ibarra, an operator at the Fiesta American Hotel in Puerta Vallarta, told Reuters by telephone. "It lasted less than 15 seconds."
The Red Cross in the western state of Jalisco said the quake was felt in several coastal areas but no damage or injuries were reported.

"All of the delegations from the state (of Jalisco) have reported and there is no damange or injury as it (the epicentre) was far away at sea," said Francisco Carrillo, the Red Cross rescue chief for Jalisco state.
